## Triage: routed and graded — **`domain:spec`** · **p2** · **`Bug`**

Triage seat (objectstack#6015), `session_01U6nJJSVZb476ckbRxmaMCA`, **R+251**, 2026-09-16T16:05Z. ⛔ This seat does not claim, dispatch or write code.

Disjunct ② — filed deliberately bare by the `domain:spec @ objectui` seat with routing left here, which is correct practice.

- **`domain:spec`** — anchoring rule: the change lands on the platform element schemas in **`packages/spec`**. ⭐ Routed by **fix site**, ⛔ not by the word `ui` in the card's title prefix, which would have mis-routed it to a rendering lane. The objectui mirror is the *second* half of the ruling and belongs to that repo's own lane.
- **`type: Bug`** — 违背已声明契约: `ComponentPropsMap` **refuses `navigation` by name** on the `object-kanban` and `object-calendar` faces while objectui's renderers **read and honour it**, and `object-timeline` has no entry at all. Declaration and runtime disagree, in the direction where the author's correct-looking metadata is refused at the door.
- **`priority:p2`** — it executes a **maintainer ruling** (objectui#8652, reply verbatim `B`), and it is the **upstream half**: the objectui mirror cannot land until the platform schema declares `navigation`, so this card gates work in a second repository. ⛔ Not p1 — no shipped surface is broken today and nothing is user-facing.

⚠️ For the claiming seat: option **B** was chosen and A / C / D were explicitly **not** taken — ⛔ do not re-open the option set. Declaring a key on a published schema is accept-set growth ⇒ expect **`Clause-②: yes`**; that declaration is the claiming seat's, ⛔ not this one's.

<sub>本评论来自分诊座位</sub>

## Why this card is picked now, stated so it can be overruled in one word

⚠️ This seat had been reading `docs/NORTH-STAR.md` 「优先级」 item 3 as 「p2/p3 全挡」 while product P0/P1 are open. That is an **over-reading, and this claim corrects it**: the sentence bars p2/p3 **工具卡、契约卫生卡**, and this is neither. An author who writes `navigation` on a standalone `object-kanban` / `object-calendar` board gets the behaviour they asked for from the renderer and a **by-name refusal** from the platform — a capability that cannot be written down. Three objectui cards (objectui#8652 / #8654 / #8651's `CalendarSchema` arm) are `pm:blocked` behind it.

⛔ The option set is **not** reopened. objectui#8652 was ruled **B** (verbatim `B`); A, C and D were explicitly not taken, and triage's grading repeats that instruction. This round executes B and nothing else.

## Tier derivation, quoted from this act's own run

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --tier packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts packages/spec/src/ui/react-blocks.ts` (exit 0), verbatim:

> Model tier — no path-derived mandate: the surface hits none of the 3 declared glob(s), derived here, not recalled.
> Clause ② SUSPECT surface — a hint, not a verdict: judge the tier from the card CONTENT as best you can … whichever tier is dispatched, the PR's actual diff passes the clause-② enqueue gate before the card may enqueue.
> - packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts ⇢ 'packages/spec/src/**' — the contract surface … the normal landing zone of a clause-② card

⇒ `Clause-②: yes` is declared because declaring `navigation` on two element faces and adding a third entry **widens the published accept set**. The contract review is owed at the contract tier before this card may enqueue, and this seat will raise the dual-carrier gate on the card and its PR when the PR exists.

## Prior rulings

`node scripts/pm/check-prior-rulings.mjs --card 17987` was run in this act against the corpus at `origin/main`. The governing ruling is **not** in that corpus — it is objectui#8652's maintainer reply, quoted verbatim on this card's face and endorsed by triage `5700608500`. ⛔ This seat did not re-derive the ADR hits and does not endorse them.

## Contract review **FAIL** — one BLOCKING finding, and it is this card's own defect shape reproduced on a new face. **One rework round**, ⛔ not an escalation.

Seat `domain:spec#4` (`session_01AmH9bKvGoLjiY86Q4Z3og2`), read and written at 2026-09-20T00:28Z. Review of record: PR #19219 comment `5746400707`, `Served-tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, `Head-sha: 02d81323c9324f83053b85f8e1970c28ca4903c1`, **VERDICT: FAIL**. The dual-carrier gate is stripped in one stroke from this card and from PR #19219 — ⛔ the strip is **not** a clearance; the FAIL record itself is what blocks the landing.

### The BLOCKING finding, re-verified by this seat rather than accepted

⛔ This seat does not take a FAIL at face value any more than a PASS. Re-read on the PR head in this act:

| reading | value |
|---|---|
| the new `ObjectTimelinePropsSchema` row | declares **14** keys — `objectName` `timeline` `filter` `sort` `limit` `items` `variant` `dateFormat` `rowLabel` `minDate` `maxDate` `descriptionField` `mapping` `navigation`. **`data` is not among them.** |
| `ObjectKanbanPropsSchema` — untouched by this PR | `data: z.array(z.unknown()).optional().describe('Static inline cards — bypasses the object query')` |
| `ObjectCalendarPropsSchema` — untouched by this PR | `data: z.array(z.unknown()).optional().describe('Pre-fetched records — skips the internal fetch')` |

The reviewer's half, which this seat did not re-run and therefore relays as the reviewer's reading: `ObjectTimeline.tsx:171/247/256` reads `(props as any).data`; a runtime probe at the `.objectui-sha` pin through `SchemaRenderer` and the real registry renders the authored row from `properties.data` and **never calls `dataSource.find`**, while the control without `data` calls `find` and renders no such row (2/2). The lint gate raises `component-props-unknown-key` on `properties.data` for `object-timeline` and raises nothing for the identical kanban/calendar nodes.

⇒ **an author who writes `data` on a standalone timeline gets the behaviour they asked for from the renderer and a by-name refusal from the platform.** That sentence is this card's own opening paragraph. The row this PR adds is the first thing ever to judge `object-timeline`, so the refusal is **minted here**, not inherited — a face that previously refused nothing now refuses a key its renderer honours.

### Why this is a rework and ⛔ not a decision for the maintainer

The reviewer offered two exits: declare `data`, or obtain a ruling that it is host-only. **The second is not needed and this seat says so rather than passing the cost upward:** the two sibling object-bound faces in the same file already declare `data` with exactly the skip-the-fetch semantics, and this PR leaves both untouched. Declaring it on the third face is **consistency with the siblings**, not a new contract question. It also stays inside the arm this PR already declared (`Clause-②: yes`, widening) — no new accept-set question is opened.

⛔ The ruling's option set is still closed. This changes nothing about objectui#8652's `B`.

### The remedy, scoped by this seat

1. Declare `data` on `ObjectTimelinePropsSchema` **matching the sibling faces' shape** — `z.array(z.unknown()).optional()` — with a `.describe()` held to what the timeline renderer actually does with it. ⛔ Do not invent a different shape for the third face; that would fork the vocabulary the same way a second `navigation` dialect would have.
2. Extend the test battery: the row **accepts** `data`, and the bogus-key control still fires on the same face through `unrecognized_keys`.
3. Carry it into the changeset's key list and the PR body's timeline key set — the body currently publishes a refusal that is about to stop being true.
4. Regenerate the artefacts the change moves.

### What PASSED, recorded so the rework does not re-open it

Items 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 of the review all passed on measurement: widening only (46 untouched faces byte-identical as control), the shared-def identity pin **discriminates a behaviourally identical fork** (fork ablation: 1 failed / 10 passed, exactly the identity test), the view-level carrier untouched, the reverse verification reproduced independently (leg A: 5 failed / 6 passed, matching the implementer), the out-of-surface files verified as genuinely forced, and the changeset level correct. ⛔ None of that is re-litigated in the rework.

### Noted, ⛔ not in this rework

- `timeline.metaFields` (read at `ObjectTimeline.tsx:332-334`) is refused by the shared `TimelineConfigSchema` — the same shape on the **view** face, pre-existing, and a separate card. ⚠️ Together with the two findings the implementer reported (`object-grid`/`object-gantt`/`object-tree` declaring `navigation` as `z.unknown()`, and the `timeline.dateField` alias), **three carded-shaped findings from this round have no card**: this seat cannot open issues in this session, and that gap is on the maintainer's desk.
- `variant: 'gantt'` is declared though the composed path refuses it with a named diagnostic — documented, not a silent drop.

<sub>Every reading in the table above was taken in the act that wrote this comment, at the clock on its opening line; the runtime-probe and lint-gate readings are the reviewer's and are labelled as such.</sub>
